rationale: Full-text Spanish article analyzing territorial marginalization and unequal water access between Mexico City (CDMX) and peripheral municipalities of the State of Mexico in the Metropolitan Zone of the Valley of Mexico (ZMVM), with a neo-institutional analysis and a newspaper-archive case study of water protests in Ecatepec (2018-2020). The dominant mechanism family is institutional_structure_coordination: the paper centers on centralized water transfers (Lerma/Cutzamala) favoring the capital over peripheral extraction/conurbation municipalities, incomplete municipalization since 1983 (delegation and deconcentration without fiscal/technical decentralization for municipalities and CDMX alcaldías), and intergovernmental partisan friction between federal, state (CAEM), capital, and municipal (SAPASE) authorities. Politicized clientelistic rationing and discretionary supply manipulation (discretion_accommodation) are also analyzed as a secondary mechanism in Ecatepec. Outcomes span both effective_access (water scarcity, supply cuts/intermittency, quantity/quality deficits, and reliance on pipas tracked in the Ecatepec protest analysis) and primary_connection (household piped-water network availability mapped across ZMVM concentric rings using INEGI 2015 data), warranting 'multiple' for assigned_outcome_label_with_multiple with effective_access as primary_outcome_family. Study design is qualitative (documentary review, neo-institutional analysis, descriptive census mapping, and a hemerographic case study).
